negative_findings.description: No parent group in this cell publishes a Czech-language investor-relations channel. Searches in Czech for group results returned only (a) subsidiary press rooms relaying the group release, and (b) Czech financial media. Erste, KBC, SG, UniCredit, RBI and BNP Paribas all report in English (plus German/Dutch/French for their home markets).
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero parent-group IR pages found in Czech. The only cs-language primary artefacts in this cell are Erste releases republished on csas.cz, Czech-language prospectuses on rb.cz and ppfbanka.cz, and pse.cz issuer pages for the dual-listed Erste Group Bank AG.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any collection design that keys on Czech-language discovery will systematically miss this entire channel. Conversely, cs-language terms are still needed to find the relay layer and the Czech-law prospectus documents, so a bilingual crawl is mandatory rather than optional.

negative_findings.description: BNP Paribas group reporting appears to no longer carry a Czech retail-banking segment. Hello bank! by Cetelem (launched in CZ in November 2017) closed Czech current and savings accounts in 2023 and transferred its active loan book to Česká spořitelna.
negative_findings.result_summary: No BNP Paribas Personal Finance Czech standalone results or segment disclosure located. Remaining Czech presence found is Cardif pojišťovna, Arval, Leasing Solutions, Securities Services and a corporate/institutional banking branch — visible only as entity-list entries, not as a reported segment.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: BNP Paribas should be de-prioritised relative to the other five parents in this cell; tracking it at URD-annex frequency (annual) is sufficient, and expecting quarterly Czech banking data from it would waste collection budget.

negative_findings.description: UniCredit's 'Financial Reports from our Countries' index returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on direct fetch. The same host serves /content/dam/ PDF assets that were referenced successfully from search results.
negative_findings.result_summary: 403 with no response body, 2026-08-25. Treated as a bot/WAF defence hypothesis, not as a dead or removed page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should retry this with browser-class headers before any liveness verdict; recording it as dead would wrongly remove the group-maintained pointer to UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia's statutory reporting.

negative_findings.description: Two guessed hub URLs failed: societegenerale.com/en/analysts-investors returned 404 and rbinternational.com/en/raiffeisen/about-us/our-network/international-network.html returned 404.
negative_findings.result_summary: SG's IR content actually lives on a separate host, investors.societegenerale.com, which was located and fetched successfully. For RBI, no HTML index page for the country sheets was found — only the direct PDF asset under /content/dam/.../country-sheets-2025/.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that hub URLs must be discovered from search or site navigation, never constructed. It also means RBI country-sheet editions have no discoverable index and will need year-segment probing or site-search to detect new releases.

negative_findings.description: Erste Group's Capital Markets Days page yielded only a link to CMD2019; no recent capital-markets-day deck for the current strategy cycle was located, despite the cell rationale specifically naming CMD decks as a source of Czech digital-investment plans.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recent strategy content (2030 ambition, five pillars, CZ retail loan share 27.0% / deposit share 27.5%) was found instead inside the quarterly results decks and third-party slide summaries, not in a CMD deck.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Strategy-level Czech numbers currently have to be mined from quarterly presentations rather than from a dedicated CMD artefact. The CMD page should still be watched, but it cannot be the primary route to digital-investment and branch-plan data today.

negative_findings.description: For the ATM/self-service hardware and services parents (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Nexi), no Czech-specific disclosure was found in group financial reporting.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only marketing artefacts surfaced — e.g. a Diebold Nixdorf customer case study on end-to-end ATM network outsourcing for ČSOB (99.8% uptime, 99.98% cash availability). Nexi produced no Czech-specific hit at all.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For these vendors the useful group-level channel is case studies and press releases, not segment reporting. They belong in a vendor/supplier cell rather than in parent-group investor reporting, and should not be tracked here at earnings cadence.

negative_findings.description: Société Générale publishes no Czech- or Komerční banka-specific investor deck. KB is folded into the international retail banking / mobility and financial services reporting line.
negative_findings.result_summary: No SG 'Czech Republic' segment slide located. The recoverable KB-level detail sits in the quarterly financial series Excel supplement and the URD's country-by-country annex, not in a dedicated presentation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations: for SG, extraction must target Excel supplements and URD annexes. Searching for a KB deck that does not exist would burn effort; SG's KB detail is also thinner than Erste's or KBC's Czech disclosure.

coverage_gaps.description: Virtually all Czech-segment data in this cell is locked inside PDFs (quarterly reports, presentation decks, URDs, country sheets). Only Erste (XLSX data sheets), KBC (results table / ESEF XBRL), RBI (XLSM) and SG (quarterly series) offer structured alternatives.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Prioritise the structured artefacts as the primary series feed and use PDFs only for narrative. Build a PDF table-extraction step specifically tuned to the KBC 'Czech Republic Business Unit' chapter and the Erste 'Czech Republic' segment tables, which are the two densest recurring sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language coverage of this cell is structurally thin, as documented in the negative findings. cs-language terms were successfully used and did surface the relay layer and Czech-law prospectuses, but no parent publishes IR content in Czech.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Accept English as the primary language for this cell and use cs only for (a) subsidiary press-room relays, (b) prospectus/mandatory-disclosure trees on rb.cz, ppfbanka.cz, unicreditbank.cz, and (c) pse.cz / CNB issuer registers. Maintain a cs↔en glossary so the same event can be matched across both layers.

coverage_gaps.description: The CRD Article 89 country-by-country reporting annexes — which give Czech Republic turnover, profit before tax, tax paid and FTE headcount on a uniform basis across Erste, KBC, SG, UniCredit, RBI and BNP Paribas — were reasoned about and are known to sit in group annual reports/URDs, but the specific annex pages were not individually located and page-anchored in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each of the six groups, open the current annual report/URD and record the exact section title and page anchor for the country-by-country annex. This yields the single most directly comparable cross-parent Czech dataset in the whole cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical depth was only established for Erste (reports reportedly back to 1997) and Euronet (EDGAR filings back to at least 2004). Archive depth for KBC, SG, UniCredit, RBI, PPF and Worldline was not determined.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a one-off backfill probe per parent against both the corporate IR archive and the relevant officially appointed mechanism (OeKB for AT, FSMA/STORI for BE, AMF/BDIF for FR, CONSOB eMarket for IT, AFM for NL) to establish the earliest retrievable year before committing to a time-series design.

coverage_gaps.description: Only the Austrian OAM (OeKB) was identified and verified. The equivalent statutory archives for the Belgian (KBC), French (SG, BNP Paribas, Worldline), Italian (UniCredit) and Dutch (PPF's former N.V. entities) parents were not located in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Identify and add the Belgian FSMA, French AMF, Italian CONSOB/eMarket Storage and Dutch AFM regulated-information repositories as durable archive pointers, mirroring the role OeKB plays for Erste and RBI.

coverage_gaps.description: Two perimeter/identity changes in this cell threaten archive continuity: PPF Group N.V. became PPF GROUP a.s., and PPF Financial Holdings B.V. became PPF Financial Holdings a.s. Erste's acquisition of Santander Bank Polska (now Erste Bank Polska) also changes the segment mix against which the Czech segment is compared.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Record entity-identity mappings (old name, new name, jurisdiction, first/last reporting period) so time series are not silently broken, and flag Erste segment comparisons that straddle the Poland consolidation.

coverage_gaps.description: Two access frictions were observed or inferred: unicreditgroup.eu HTML pages appear WAF-protected (403), and the most analytically useful third-party layers (Patria research, Seeking Alpha, Quartr) are paywalled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Provision a browser-class fetcher with realistic headers for WAF-protected issuer sites, and treat paywalled research as out of scope for automated collection — rely on issuer-published webcast replays and free transcript feeds instead.

brief: Every systemic Czech bank in scope reports upward into a foreign parent, and the parent's investor-reporting stack is a genuinely separate channel: English-language, quarter-driven, and substantially richer on Czech volumes, market shares, cost/income and digital plans than the local entity's own disclosure. The densest sources are Erste Group (Czech Republic geographic segment plus an XLSX data-sheet workbook), KBC (a dedicated 'Czech Republic Business Unit' chapter in every quarterly report, on a stable CDN URL pattern), and RBI (Central Europe segment, XLSM data, and a one-page group-authored Czech country sheet); SG and UniCredit are thinner and require mining Excel supplements, URD country-by-country annexes and CEE decks, while PPF is unlisted and discloses through consolidated annual accounts, sub-holding reports and arranger-hosted bond prospectuses. Payments extends the cell usefully — Worldline (KB SmartPay), Euronet and Global Payments all disclose Czech acquiring, ATM and processing detail at group level, with the US filers giving the most granular and most machine-readable archive. The principal constraints are that almost none of this exists in Czech (only subsidiary press-room relays, Czech-law prospectuses and pse.cz issuer pages do), and that most numbers sit inside PDFs, so collection should key on the structured artefacts first and treat the OeKB-style statutory archives as the durable completeness backstop.
